title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: RAG retrieves passages from a knowledge base and adds them to the prompt so a language model can ground its answer in source documents and reduce hallucination.

title: Chunking documents for RAG
text: Splitting documents into overlapping chunks of a few hundred tokens improves retrieval recall; chunks that are too large dilute relevance, chunks that are too small lose context.

title: BM25 ranking
text: BM25 is a lexical ranking function that scores documents by term frequency, inverse document frequency and document length normalisation controlled by k1 and b.

title: Dense embeddings
text: Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into embedding vectors and ranks by cosine similarity, which captures synonyms that keyword search misses.

title: Hybrid search
text: Hybrid search combines sparse BM25 and dense embedding results, often with reciprocal rank fusion, to get both exact keyword matches and semantic matches.

title: Reciprocal rank fusion
text: Reciprocal rank fusion sums 1 / (k + rank) across ranked lists, so it merges retrievers without calibrating their scores.

title: Evaluating retrieval
text: Recall at k, mean reciprocal rank and nDCG measure whether relevant passages are retrieved and how high they rank.

title: Measuring hallucination
text: Faithfulness checks whether each claim in a generated answer is supported by the retrieved context; unsupported claims are counted as hallucinations.

title: Vector databases
text: Vector databases such as Pinecone, FAISS and pgvector store embeddings and answer approximate nearest neighbour queries at low latency.

title: Reranking
text: A cross-encoder reranker rescores the top retrieved passages jointly with the query, improving precision at the cost of extra latency.

title: Docker containers
text: Docker packages an application and its dependencies into an image that runs the same way on a laptop, in CI and in production.

title: Kubernetes basics
text: Kubernetes schedules containers across a cluster, restarts failed pods and scales deployments horizontally based on load.

title: CI/CD pipelines
text: Continuous integration runs tests on every commit; continuous delivery automatically builds and deploys artifacts once the tests pass, for example with GitHub Actions.

title: REST API design
text: A REST API exposes resources over HTTP with clear verbs, status codes, pagination and versioning; FastAPI generates OpenAPI docs from type hints.

title: OAuth 2.0
text: OAuth 2.0 lets a user grant an application limited access to another service using access tokens and refresh tokens instead of sharing a password.

title: SQL indexing
text: Database indexes such as B-trees speed up lookups and joins; too many indexes slow down writes, so index the columns used in filters and joins.

title: Caching
text: A cache such as Redis stores frequently read results in memory to cut latency and database load; invalidation strategy decides when entries expire.

title: Horizontal scaling
text: Horizontal scaling adds more stateless service instances behind a load balancer, while vertical scaling gives one machine more CPU and memory.

title: Observability
text: Observability combines logs, metrics and traces so engineers can monitor latency, error rates and saturation and debug production incidents.

title: Unit vs integration tests
text: Unit tests check one function in isolation; integration tests exercise several components together such as an API handler and its database.

title: Overfitting
text: A model overfits when it memorises training data and performs poorly on new data; regularisation, more data and early stopping reduce overfitting.

title: Cross-validation
text: K-fold cross-validation trains and evaluates a model k times on different splits to estimate generalisation performance more reliably.

title: Precision and recall
text: Precision is the share of predicted positives that are correct; recall is the share of actual positives the model finds; F1 is their harmonic mean.

title: Gradient descent
text: Gradient descent updates model parameters in the direction that reduces the loss; the learning rate controls the step size.

title: Transformers and attention
text: Transformers use self-attention to weigh every token against every other token, which lets language models capture long-range context.

title: Fine-tuning vs prompting
text: Fine-tuning updates model weights on task data, while prompting and retrieval change only the input; RAG is cheaper to keep up to date than fine-tuning.

title: Prompt injection
text: Prompt injection hides instructions inside retrieved documents or user input to hijack an LLM; treat retrieved text as data and restrict tool permissions.

title: AI agents
text: An AI agent lets a language model plan, call tools and observe results in a loop until a task is done, which needs guardrails, evaluation and logging.

title: Latency budgets
text: End-to-end latency for a RAG request is the sum of embedding, retrieval, reranking and generation time, so each stage needs its own budget.

title: A/B testing
text: An A/B test randomly splits users between a control and a variant and uses a statistical test to decide whether the change improved the metric.
